A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 2DMamba work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material. Content can be reliably matched across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original WSI classification, survival prediction, natural-image evaluation, computational-efficiency measurements, and ablation results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds architectural comparisons and classification standard deviations.

M1.justification: The proposed horizontal-then-vertical scan, shared A parameter, learnable non-tissue token, MIL architecture, and fused scanning algorithm remain unchanged. Expanded aggregator and CUDA descriptions disclose existing details; alternative configurations are evaluated as ablations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five WSI classification datasets, five survival datasets, ImageNet-1K classification, and ADE20K segmentation. The added ablations use retained datasets without introducing new tasks or test environments.

E2.justification: v2 adds MambaMIL variants using two-direction, four-direction raster, and four-direction cross scans in Table 7. Table S5 also adds a naive 2D comparator to WSI accuracy evaluation, beyond its earlier efficiency comparison. The main MIL and natural-image comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New ablations introduce controls varying scan directions and shared versus independent A. Tables 4 and S2 revise the reported VMamba-T and 2DVMamba-T parameter counts from 31M to 30M, without establishing a redesign or rerun. Existing splits, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands architectural validation: Table 7 tests multidirectional scanning, Table S3 tests parameter sharing across five classification datasets, and Table S5 tests a naive row-then-column alternative. Earlier padding, positional-embedding, scan-order, depth, and dimension ablations remain; the positional-embedding study moves to Table S4.

E5.justification: v1 reports five-seed classification means without dispersion. v2 adds standard deviations for every method, dataset, and metric in that main classification comparison through Table S10. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting; the five-run count is retained, with no stated increase in runs or added significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for multidirectional scanning, parameter sharing, naive 2D scanning, and classification variability. For example, Table 7 reports PANDA accuracy of 0.4939 for four-direction cross scanning versus 0.5075 for 2DMambaMIL. Tables 4/S2 also change Swin-T ImageNet accuracy from 80.5% to 81.3% and Vim-S from 80.5% to 80.3%. Retained primary WSI, survival, segmentation, and efficiency results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Supplement C newly derives the existing two-dimensional state expansion through intermediate horizontal and vertical sums in Eqs. (11)–(16). v1 states the resulting Eq. (7) without these derivation steps. The underlying recurrences and memory-complexity argument remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly claims to be the first intrinsic 2D Mamba method with an efficient parallel algorithm and strengthens the introduction's assertion that multidirectional flattening necessarily loses spatial structure. The abstract's contributions, application scope, and reported performance improvements remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds a parameter-sharing rationale and acknowledges the absence of an optimality guarantee, attributes multidirectional scanning limitations to incomplete cell-interaction modelling, and interprets standard deviations as evidence of stability. Its new claim that parameter-sharing variants differ within ±1% is inconsistent with several Table S3 entries.

D1.justification: Supplements A–B substantially expand reproducibility information: non-overlapping 512×512 patches, CLAM tissue preprocessing, UNI architecture, aggregator equations and dimensions, 16×16/32×32 tiles, boundary padding values, and 64-thread assignments. These are newly documented details rather than established implementation changes. Existing training settings and the code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including Brain Diffuser, MedPrompt, a remote-sensing survey, VLEER, DINOv2, and Multi-scale VMamba, while removing Kurek's 2D-system reference. It also sharpens its novelty positioning against methods retaining the vanilla 1D CUDA scanner. The related-work discussion otherwise remains largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 revises the introduction and scan explanation, moves implementation details into Supplement A, replaces numbered result subsubsections with paragraph headings, and reorganizes the appendices. Author-affiliation notes and acknowledgments also change. The overall narrative structure and much existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds tables for the new comparisons and standard deviations, relocates the original positional-embedding Table 7 to Table S4, and redraws Figure 4 while retaining its qualitative example. Figure 1's caption and several placements change. Other principal diagrams and all seven supplementary qualitative figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility and evidential transparency through practical preprocessing/CUDA details, new architectural controls, and standard deviations for retained classification results. The gains are tempered by imprecise new interpretations: Supplement G claims parameter-sharing differences remain within ±1%, whereas Table S3 reports BRACS F1 values of 0.6786 and 0.7045, a 2.59-percentage-point gap.
